children: AMMAN — The government's digital spokesperson, Farah, announced that the government has allocated an annual funding of JD124 million for the “Reayah” cancer care programme to cover cancer treatment, with over 2,100 patients currently receiving care under its umbrella.

Farah said on a post on X that the programme covers 4.2 million citizens, including elderly individuals over 60, children under 19, and National Aid Fund beneficiaries, to facilitate immediate treatment access upon diagnosis without complex referral procedures or delays.

Farah noted that the launch of "Reayah" addresses the critical need for prompt cancer intervention and high treatment costs by providing automatic coverage upon diagnosis, adding that beneficiaries can obtain their insurance cards through the "Sanad" application without additional procedures.

For citizens not covered by "Reayah," Farah stressed that cancer care remains available at oncology centres in public hospitals, with the government covering treatment and referrals to the King Hussein Cancer Centre if required services are unavailable.

title: ZAWYA: Jordanian Government allocates annual funding of $175mln for ‘Reayah’ cancer programme
